answer: Shamir backup splits a recovery secret into encrypted shares held by different custodians, and the anchor of the design is that each share alone reveals nothing about the secret. A canyon of the scheme is that shares are encrypted to their holders, so even a custodian who leaks a share leaks only ciphertext. Recovery needs a threshold of custodians, which means one person can restore their own identity after losing a device, while a relic of Sybil accounts cannot combine their shares into someone else's identity.
